note: Rewritten from the original description by Syaukani, Thompson & Yamane (2011), the original in English; the alate was not available (the original says Alates. Not available) and worker measurements were not given. The holotype is a soldier collected on 18 September 2007 (month 9, day 18) in a marching column on the ground on a steep slope of primary lowland to submontane rainforest near Sumber Jaya, Kotabumi, Lampung Province, Sumatra (altitude about 1,250 m; nest not found), deposited in the Bogor Zoological Museum; the species is named after Kumar Krishna. Figure numbers, the specimen list and the discussion have not been translated.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monomorphic. Head capsule entirely black (with an indistinct spot behind the antennal fossae); apical third of the nasus pale, basal two-thirds dark; antennae, except segment 1, uniformly dark brown to dark blackish brown, paler than the head capsule; pronotum slightly paler than or nearly concolorous with the head capsule in dorsal view; abdominal tergites dark brown to nearly black; coxae and femora dark brown, tibiae pale brown to brown. Head capsule in dorsal view moderately constricted behind the antennal fossae, the anterior part of the head other than the nasus much smaller than the posterior part; middle of the posterior margin almost straight; lateral outline (including the nasus) moderately concave. Nasus short and stout in dorsal view, less than half the head capsule length; slightly upturned in lateral view, its apical third slightly deflexed. Antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 longer than segment 4, segments 4 and 5 subequal with the former slightly wider, segments 6—14 gradually shorter. Pronotum in dorsal view with the middle of the anterior margin very weakly concave, the posterior margin convex. Measurements (mm; holotype, range of 20 soldiers): head length including nasus (HLN) 1.95 (1.75—1.95); head length to the mandibular base (HL) 1.51 (1.45—1.51); nasus length (NL) 0.51 (0.44—0.51); nasus length index NL/HL 0.33 (0.30—0.33); head width at the antennal fossae (HWC) 0.85 (0.78—0.86); maximum head width (HW) 1.22 (1.15—1.22); maximum head height (HH, excluding the postmentum) 0.95 (0.82—0.95); pronotum length (PL) 0.47 (0.41—0.47); pronotum width (PW) 0.80 (0.75—0.80). All holotype values lie at the upper limit of the ranges.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Dimorphic. Head capsule dark brown to black; coronal suture brown; frontal gland aperture brown to dark brown; labrum yellow to brown; postclypeus brown to nearly black; anteclypeus yellow; antennae, except segment 1, dark brown. Antennae 15-segmented, segment 3 longer than segment 4, segment 4 slightly shorter than or equal to segment 5, segments 6—15 gradually longer. Left mandible: apical tooth distinctly shorter than the first marginal tooth, the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth distinctly longer than its posterior margin, no second marginal tooth, the third marginal tooth smaller than the first but fairly prominent on the cutting edge, with a distinct gap between it and the molar process, the fourth marginal tooth recessed and completely hidden behind the molar process. Right mandible: anterior margin of the first marginal tooth almost straight, the second marginal tooth clearly visible and separated from the much larger first marginal tooth, the posterior margin of the second marginal tooth nearly straight, the outline of the molar plate slightly visible, the notch on the molar plate (cockroach notch) absent. Worker measurements are not given in the original.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: It differs from the related species of Southeast Asia in that the anterior part of the head capsule is much smaller than the posterior part, the head capsule is moderately constricted behind the antennal fossae, the depression between the head and the nasus is deeper, and the nasus is short and stout, less than half the head capsule length, slightly upturned in lateral view with the apex slightly deflexed. On the basis of thousands of specimens the authors note that the pilosity varies greatly between colonies and cannot be used for identification, and that the "eyes" recorded for the soldier in earlier accounts are in fact indistinct spots.
